evidence.claim: CPJ urged Marcos to stop red-tagging journalists, allow access to Rappler reporter Lian Buan, restore ABS-CBN's franchise, drop charges against Frenchie Cumpio, and address impunity in journalist killings.
evidence.title: CPJ calls on president-elect Marcos to protect press freedom in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: CPJ urged Marcos to stop red-tagging journalists, allow access to Rappler reporter Lian Buan, restore ABS-CBN's franchise, drop charges against Frenchie Cumpio, and address impunity in journalist killings.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and the recommendations section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct advocacy letter from a major press-freedom monitor with specific contemporaneous concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: President-elect Marcos was the addressee; this is a warning about expected risk, not proof of later conduct.
contrary_evidence: This is a warning letter, so it is predictive and advisory rather than descriptive of implemented policy.

evidence.claim: HRW said the human rights situation hardly changed after Marcos took office, that unlawful force in the drug war continued, at least 90 drug-related killings were counted through September 30, and red-tagging of activists persisted.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Philippines
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the human rights situation hardly changed after Marcos took office, that unlawful force in the drug war continued, at least 90 drug-related killings were counted through September 30, and red-tagging of activists persisted.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major independent monitoring source summarizing the year-end human-rights picture with specific allegations and counts.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 and the first months of Marcos's rule.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Assesses Marcos-era conditions; the killings and red-tagging are not all individually traced to presidential order, so attribution is mixed and partly institutional.
contrary_evidence: HRW is an advocacy monitor, so its conclusions should be weighed against official claims and other independent reporting.

evidence.claim: The report says red-tagging continued under the new administration, the NTF-ELCAC remained the primary actor, and the Marcos administration's position on red-tagging was unclear.
evidence.title: Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines, 2022
evidence.excerpt: The report says red-tagging continued under the new administration, the NTF-ELCAC remained the primary actor, and the Marcos administration's position on red-tagging was unclear.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual country report summarizing the 2022 human-rights environment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022, published after the year-end reporting cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Describes conditions under the Marcos administration; the practice itself is partly inherited and partly tolerated, not fully individualized.
contrary_evidence: This is a broad annual assessment, so it does not isolate a single presidential order or decision.

evidence.claim: In May, about 200 human rights advocates protesting the proclamation were blocked by police, some were struck with truncheons and shields, at least 10 were wounded, and the Commission on Human Rights opened an investigation.
evidence.title: Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines, 2022
evidence.excerpt: In May, about 200 human rights advocates protesting the proclamation were blocked by police, some were struck with truncheons and shields, at least 10 were wounded, and the Commission on Human Rights opened an investigation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual country report citing a specific protest-dispersal incident and subsequent review.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to protest treatment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Police conduct under the Marcos-era state, though operational decisions were mediated through the police chain of command.
contrary_evidence: This was a specific incident, not proof of nationwide systematic terror.
The report does not show Marcos personally ordered the use of force.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said red-tagging continued under the Marcos administration against human rights defenders, activists, development workers, and other targeted groups.
evidence.title: Philippines: Authorities must end red-tagging, attacks on rights defenders
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said red-tagging continued under the Marcos administration against human rights defenders, activists, development workers, and other targeted groups.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major international rights monitor summarizing a continuing pattern after Marcos took office.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 and the early Marcos period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Assesses Marcos-era continuation of a broader state-linked practice, though not every instance is directly presidentially ordered.
contrary_evidence: This is advocacy reporting and should be checked against official and other independent sources.

evidence.claim: Marcos ordered an investigation into Percy Lapid's killing and instructed the Palace to review the conduct of the probe.
evidence.title: Marcos orders probe into Percy Lapid slay
evidence.excerpt: Marcos ordered an investigation into Percy Lapid's killing and instructed the Palace to review the conduct of the probe.
evidence.source_locator: article body and quoted remarks from the president
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government wire reporting a direct presidential response to a major journalist killing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and immediately after the killing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos response after the fact; it shows remedial action, not prevention.
contrary_evidence: A reactive investigation does not erase the underlying risk environment.

evidence.claim: For Marcos's first SONA, police said the right to peaceful assembly would be recognized, protesters would face maximum tolerance, freedom parks would be available, and Batasan Road was a no-rally zone.
evidence.title: SONA protest route, freedom parks and maximum tolerance reminders issued by police
evidence.excerpt: For Marcos's first SONA, police said the right to peaceful assembly would be recognized, protesters would face maximum tolerance, freedom parks would be available, and Batasan Road was a no-rally zone.
evidence.source_locator: article body and police guidance summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government wire on security rules for a major public event under Marcos's administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Police guidance during Marcos's first SONA; operationally relevant but not a direct presidential order in the source.
contrary_evidence: The no-rally zone and heavy police framing also show a restrictive security posture.
The source does not prove how the rules were applied in every case.

evidence.claim: Congress, sitting as the National Board of Canvassers, proclaimed Ferdinand Marcos Jr. president-elect on May 25, 2022 after the fastest canvassing in Philippine election history.
evidence.title: Marcos, Duterte proclaimed winners in PH’s fastest vote count
evidence.excerpt: Congress, sitting as the National Board of Canvassers, proclaimed Ferdinand Marcos Jr. president-elect on May 25, 2022 after the fastest canvassing in Philippine election history.
evidence.source_locator: article body and headline; proclamation passage
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government newswire reporting the formal proclamation and vote count.
evidence.period_fit: Directly precedes Marcos's entry into office in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Marks the lawful transfer into Marcos's presidency; not proof of democratic quality by itself.
contrary_evidence: A formal proclamation does not establish that the campaign was fully fair or uncontested.

evidence.claim: Marcos took his oath as the 17th president on June 30, 2022 and promised to promote unity and bring progress to the country.
evidence.title: Marcos Jr. sworn in as PH's 17th president
evidence.excerpt: Marcos took his oath as the 17th president on June 30, 2022 and promised to promote unity and bring progress to the country.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government wire with a dated inauguration report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and the start of Marcos's term.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's assumption of office and acceptance of constitutional transfer.
contrary_evidence: The inauguration shows succession, not necessarily democratic restraint in day-to-day rule.

evidence.claim: The Carter Center said voters and domestic observer groups had general confidence in COMELEC and in candidates' willingness to accept results, but interlocutors raised concerns about disinformation, media freedom, political-economic links, and the transparency and reliability of the automated system.
evidence.title: Final Report: 2022 General Elections in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The Carter Center said voters and domestic observer groups had general confidence in COMELEC and in candidates' willingness to accept results, but interlocutors raised concerns about disinformation, media freedom, political-economic links, and the transparency and reliability of the automated system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent election expert mission with a full report on the 2022 elections.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the May 9, 2022 election, directly relevant to Marcos's accession.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is mostly about the election environment Marcos inherited and won within, not his later governing conduct.
contrary_evidence: The report is retrospective and not all concerns are uniquely attributable to Marcos personally.

evidence.claim: The Center found a higher incidence of machine problems in the 2022 elections that were locally disruptive and also found that observed precinct procedures did not effectively ensure the secrecy of the vote.
evidence.title: Final Report: 2022 General Elections in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The Center found a higher incidence of machine problems in the 2022 elections that were locally disruptive and also found that observed precinct procedures did not effectively ensure the secrecy of the vote.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent technical election assessment with specific process findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly institutional/electoral-system context; relevant to Marcos's accession but not a personal action by him.
contrary_evidence: The report says the problems did not jeopardize overall integrity, so this is a mixed rather than catastrophic finding.

evidence.claim: The Carter Center said campaign-finance rules were only partly effective, with spending caps widely viewed as too low, a mostly unregulated pre-campaign period, and weak enforcement capacity at COMELEC.
evidence.title: Final Report: 2022 General Elections in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The Carter Center said campaign-finance rules were only partly effective, with spending caps widely viewed as too low, a mostly unregulated pre-campaign period, and weak enforcement capacity at COMELEC.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent election report with detailed legal-analysis findings.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 campaign and election cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This concerns the campaign system that enabled Marcos's victory, not a personal order by him after inauguration.
contrary_evidence: The report identifies system-wide loopholes, not necessarily a Marcos-only manipulation scheme.

evidence.claim: NAMFREL said the 2022 elections went smoothly but not without issues, and it separately recorded pockets of violence and intimidation during election day.
evidence.title: NAMFREL 2022 National and Local Elections Preliminary Report
evidence.excerpt: NAMFREL said the 2022 elections went smoothly but not without issues, and it separately recorded pockets of violence and intimidation during election day.
evidence.source_locator: report page entries dated July 18 and May 9, 2022
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major Philippine election watchdog, but the accessible page is a portal to the report summary rather than the full PDF text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly about the election environment rather than Marcos's later conduct.
contrary_evidence: The accessible summary is limited and does not by itself resolve the full range of election disputes.

evidence.claim: The report said concerns over press freedom grew because Marcos held professional journalists in low regard during the campaign; it also said he barred journalists from campaign events, snubbed debates, and favored friendly influencers and a partisan TV station.
evidence.title: Philippines | 2022 Digital News Report
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence.excerpt: The report said concerns over press freedom grew because Marcos held professional journalists in low regard during the campaign; it also said he barred journalists from campaign events, snubbed debates, and favored friendly influencers and a partisan TV station.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent research report with direct, dated observations of campaign behavior and media environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Marcos's own campaign conduct and the surrounding information environment.
contrary_evidence: This is a media-research country note, not an election tribunal finding.

evidence.claim: CHR said red-tagging in recent years has led to vilification, surveillance, harassment, unlawful arrests, enforced disappearance, and killings, and it warned that government officials continued to resort to the practice.
evidence.title: Statement of the Commission on Human Rights on the attempt to trivialize and justify the dangers of red-tagging
evidence.excerpt: CHR said red-tagging in recent years has led to vilification, surveillance, harassment, unlawful arrests, enforced disappearance, and killings, and it warned that government officials continued to resort to the practice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Philippine constitutional human-rights body, dated and explicit about the harms and continuing government use.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 campaign and transition period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The statement addresses state-linked practice during the Marcos transition, though not every incident is personally ordered by Marcos.
contrary_evidence: CHR is a rights-monitoring institution, so the statement is protective rather than neutral.

evidence.claim: Marcos asked Congress to pass National Government Rightsizing, Budget Modernization, E-Government, and E-Governance measures, saying they would improve service delivery, institutional capacity, and fiscal discipline.
evidence.title: PBBM urges Congress to pass admin’s 19 priority measures
evidence.excerpt: Marcos asked Congress to pass National Government Rightsizing, Budget Modernization, E-Government, and E-Governance measures, saying they would improve service delivery, institutional capacity, and fiscal discipline.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release summarizing a first-term SONA policy program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos policy agenda, though it is legislative proposal rather than enacted reform.
contrary_evidence: These are reform proposals, not completed institutional-strengthening outcomes.

evidence.claim: CPJ said the Philippines remained 7th among the worst countries for prosecuting killers of journalists, with 14 unsolved journalist murders, and warned that impunity could continue under Marcos after the killing of Percy Lapid.
evidence.title: Philippines still among worst countries in prosecuting killers of journalists - CPJ
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said the Philippines remained 7th among the worst countries for prosecuting killers of journalists, with 14 unsolved journalist murders, and warned that impunity could continue under Marcos after the killing of Percy Lapid.
evidence.source_locator: article body and quoted CPJ report summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent local report on a major press-freedom index and its Marcos-era implications.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and after the Percy Lapid killing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects the Marcos-era environment, though the murders themselves are not all directly attributed to him.
contrary_evidence: The DOJ response quoted in the article shows at least some reactive state enforcement, but not a resolved structural fix.

evidence.claim: APHR said disinformation and red-tagging of opposition lawmakers increased alarmingly ahead of the May 2022 polls, and that Leni Robredo was the prime target of intensified disinformation and red-tagging in social media.
evidence.title: Disinformation, red-tagging of opposition lawmakers in PH 'increased alarmingly' ahead of 2022 elections - APHR
evidence.excerpt: APHR said disinformation and red-tagging of opposition lawmakers increased alarmingly ahead of the May 2022 polls, and that Leni Robredo was the prime target of intensified disinformation and red-tagging in social media.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Regional parliamentary rights network reported through a major local outlet, but it is retrospective and third-party summarized.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly about the campaign environment that benefited Marcos, not a direct post-inauguration order by him.
contrary_evidence: Retrospective and coalition-based, so it should not be treated as a direct legal finding.

evidence.claim: ACLED recorded nearly 50 red-tagging related violent events targeting civilians between 2020 and June 30, 2023, including 13 events after Marcos took power on June 30, 2022.
evidence.title: ACLED: The communist insurgency in the Philippines: A 'protracted people’s war' continues
evidence.excerpt: ACLED recorded nearly 50 red-tagging related violent events targeting civilians between 2020 and June 30, 2023, including 13 events after Marcos took power on June 30, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Event-data organization using transparent methodology; retrospective but concrete about post-inauguration continuation.
evidence.period_fit: Spans the target year and the immediate follow-on period, so it is retrospective context rather than pure 2022 contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The events are not all personally ordered by Marcos, but they show continuity of the red-tagging environment after he assumed office.
contrary_evidence: The report covers a broader period than 2022 alone.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
